blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why a goat is considered a living thing while a stone is not? Let's explore the fascinating characteristics that distinguish living things from non-living things!

blocks.markdown: In our world, we encounter both living and non-living things every day. Living things are those that exhibit certain characteristics that define life. These characteristics include movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion, and nutrition, often summarized by the acronym MRS GREN.

blocks.title: Characteristics of Living Things
blocks.text: Living things are defined by their ability to grow, reproduce, respond to stimuli, and carry out metabolic processes.

blocks.markdown: Non-living things, on the other hand, do not possess these characteristics. For example, a stone does not grow, reproduce, or respond to its environment. In contrast, a goat can move, eat, and reproduce, which are clear signs of life.

blocks.title: Identifying Living vs Non-Living Things
blocks.prompt: Classify the following items as living or non-living: a goat, a car, a tree, and a rock.

steps.text: 1. Examine each item for characteristics of life such as growth, movement, and reproduction.
2. Determine that the goat and tree are living things, while the car and rock are non-living.

blocks.answer: The goat and tree are living things; the car and rock are non-living.

blocks.markdown: Understanding these differences is crucial in biology. It helps us appreciate the complexity of life and the environment around us.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember to use the acronym MRS GREN to recall the characteristics of living things during your exams!

points: Living things display characteristics such as movement, growth, and reproduction.
Non-living things do not exhibit these life characteristics, making them distinct from living organisms.
